notes: No investment-gold VAT exemption: Skatteetaten states investment-gold turnover is taxable and sales to private persons follow the ordinary rules; gold jewellery is 25%. Legal-tender gold coins are exempt (VAT Act s.3-6). PwC: customs duties exist only on agricultural products, foodstuffs, clothes and textiles, so gold/silver duty is 0%. No primary dealer bar list was opened, so premiums are null.

sources.name: Skatteetaten - VAT rates for purchase and sale of gold
sources.what: Rate table: 'Gold jewellery and other gold objects 25%'; gold sold by weight and fineness to businesses/public enterprises is under reverse charge (buyer calculates VAT).

sources.name: Skatteetaten - VAT Handbook M-11-1.4, domestic turnover of gold
sources.what: States turnover of investment gold in Norway is taxable, unlike most of Europe, and sales to private persons remain taxable under the ordinary rules - bullion bars take 25% VAT; gold coins that are legal tender are excluded (VAT Act s.3-6).

sources.name: PwC Tax Summaries - Norway, Corporate - Other taxes
sources.what: 'The general VAT rate is 25% and applies to all supplies of goods and services not qualifying for another rate or an exemption' (silver 25/25); 'There are no customs duties on other products than agricultural products, foodstuffs, clothes, and textile products' - import duty 0 for gold and silver.
